articleHeadline: Study Maps Hepatitis C Diversity and Drug Resistance Across Viet Nam
articleSummary: Vietnam's hepatitis C virus (HCV) epidemic is more diverse than global classifications. Genotype 2 comprised 8.5%, genotype 3 1.9%, with regional clustering: 2 in south Mekong Delta and 3 in north. Age patterns: genotype 2 patients were older (median 56) and more often female; genotype 3 were younger (median 36) and predominantly male. HIV co-infection was most frequent with genotype 1; HBV co-infection showed no genotype differences. These findings inform Vietnam's elimination efforts.

articleSummary: Nipah virus spillover from Indian flying fox (Pteropus medius) in Bangladesh frames a One Health threat linking NiV ecology with antimicrobial resistance in bat microbiota. NiV, a negative-sense RNA henipavirus, causes encephalitis and death with case-fatality rates of about 40–70% in Bangladesh, India and parts of Asia; spillover occurs via raw date palm sap contaminated by bat secretions during winter, with possible person-to-person transmission in outbreaks. P. medius ranges across South and Southeast Asia and roosts near human settlements in Bangladesh, enabling contact that drives spillover. The review also links spillover ecology to bat guano and gut microbiota carrying antimicrobial-resistance genes. In Bangladesh, reports include ESBL-producing E. coli (37%), ampicillin resistance (37%), multidrug resistance (46%); Salmonella resistance 7.9%, tetracycline 93%, nalidixic acid 86%, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim 80%. Genes blaCTX-M, blaTEM, blaSHV detected; sequencing shows broader diversity than culture. These patterns intersect deforestation, urbanization, and wastewater pollution, underscoring integrated surveillance needs.
